title: The effect of osteopathic manipulative treatment on jump height and ankle dorsiflexion in healthy amateur soccer players: A randomized controlled trial
summary: This study investigates whether osteopathic treatment can improve jump performance and ankle mobility in healthy soccer players in the short term. Participants perform jump tests and an ankle mobility test before and after a single treatment session. One group receives osteopathic treatment, while the other receives a sham treatment without therapeutic effect. The aim is to determine whether the treatment has an immediate impact on athletic performance.
conditions: Investigation of performance-related parameters (jump height and ankle mobility) in healthy, physically active participants.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Male amateur soccer players aged 18–50 years who regularly participate in training and matches (at least once per week). Participants must be free of ankle complaints, including pain, movement restrictions, or recent injuries. No diagnosed acute or chronic ankle disorders (e.g., osteoarthritis, arthritis, fractures, ligament injuries, or other structural impairments) may be present. Participants must be able to safely and fully perform the performance tests (countermovement jump and knee-to-wall test). No surgical interventions of the lower extremity within the last 6 months and no ankle injuries or structural lesions within the last 3 months are allowed. Participation in other clinical, manual therapy, or performance-related studies is not permitted. Participants must not regularly use  muscle relaxants, that could affect neuromuscular performance. Written informed consent must be obtained.
Exclusion criteria:
Regular use of muscle relaxants, that may affect neuromuscular performance. Missing or incomplete written informed consent. Self-reported inability to safely and fully perform the performance tests (countermovement jump and knee-to-wall test).
